key_concepts: The geologic time scale records Earth's history from 4.6 billion years ago to present.
It was built largely from fossil-bearing sedimentary rocks and is continually refined.
Geologic time divisions are eons, eras, periods, and epochs from largest to smallest.
Lower layers in the geologic time scale are older than layers above them.
Precambrian eons cover about 90% of Earth's history and include Hadean, Archean, and Prote
Hadean Earth was mostly molten; Archean crust cooled and simple life emerged.
Proterozoic saw single-celled organisms evolve into photosynthetic bacteria.
Phanerozoic Eon means "visible life" and contains abundant fossils.
Paleozoic Era began with sudden appearance of diverse fauna about 543 million years ago.
Mesozoic Era was dominated by dinosaurs and saw first bird and mammal fossils.
Cenozoic Era covers the past 65 million years with mammals and angiosperms dominating land
Period and epoch boundaries are often based on fossil changes, such as dinosaur extinction
